I'll leave `node_modules` in place since it's gitignored and doesn't affect anything, and `tsconfig.json`/`next-env.d.ts`/`package-lock.json` were auto-generated by the build — all normal, useful artifacts for a real Next.js project. Everything is verified working.

## Summary

The root cause of the organic-traffic problem: this SaaS pivoted from an email-cleanup product ("InboxZap") to an AI meeting assistant ("Lumina"), and the migration was left half-finished — which explains the GSC data perfectly: branded "inboxzap" queries still rank at ~position 4 (an old title tag), while every high-volume, on-brand query ranked at position 40-65 with near-zero clicks.

What I fixed in the source tree:

1. **Brand mismatch (the core bug)** — `app/layout.tsx` still served the title/description "InboxZap — Clean Your Inbox in Minutes" while every page's actual content was about Lumina, a meeting assistant. Fixed metadata to match the real product, added a title template, `metadataBase`, and Organization JSON-LD.
2. **Missing pages** — `/features` and `/pricing` existed on the live site but had no source in this repo at all. Rebuilt both with proper per-page metadata and canonical tags.
3. **Broken `/faq` redirect** — `next.config.js` redirected `/faq` → `/#faq`, but no `#faq` anchor existed anywhere, so the redirect led nowhere. Added a real FAQ section (with `FAQPage` JSON-LD) to the homepage, including an entry explicitly addressing "What happened to InboxZap?" to capture and convert the lingering branded search traffic instead of losing it to confusion.
4. **Blog was unrenderable to crawlers** — the index page was `'use client'`, fetching from a nonexistent `/api/posts` endpoint, so it rendered nothing but a loading spinner with zero crawlable links. Converted it to a server-rendered list with real `<a href>` links, and added a proper `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` with static generation, per-post metadata, and `Article` JSON-LD.
5. **Sitemap silently excluded every blog post** (a literal `TODO` left in the code). Fixed to include all posts automatically.
6. **12 blog posts entirely off-topic** — every existing post was old InboxZap content (bulk-deleting email, Gmail storage, unsubscribing from newsletters) with ~14,000 impressions but almost no clicks and no relevance to Lumina at all — pages that could never convert a visitor even if they ranked. Replaced all 12 with genuinely substantive posts targeting Lumina's actual audience (meeting recaps, async standups, action-item follow-through, meeting fatigue, etc.), cross-linked to each other and to `/features`/`/pricing`.
7. Added a generated `opengraph-image.tsx` (the old OG image path pointed at a file that never existed), and dropped the alt-text-less decorative placeholder SVGs on the homepage.

Verified the whole thing with `next build` + `next start`: all 12 posts statically generate, metadata/JSON-LD render correctly, the sitemap lists every URL, and the `/faq` redirect now lands on a real section.

One unrelated note: `next@14.2.5` has a known high/critical security advisory (flagged by `npm install`) — worth a patch bump separately from this SEO work if you want me to do that too.
